name: salesforce-commerce
_readme: Salesforce B2C Commerce Cloud as migration target (SFRA or headless over SCAPI, Business Manager, Page Designer) and as source. The source role is defensible even though the platform is multi-tenant SaaS: SFRA and SiteGenesis cartridges are a real, inspectable code base in version control with clear conventions (cartridges/, .project, app_storefront_base). Its limit is equally clear - the cartridge path, the active code version and all object metadata live in Business Manager, not in the repository. Seed from general B2C Commerce knowledge; every statement is a hypothesis until verified per engagement.

as_target.default_frontend: SFRA (Storefront Reference Architecture, server-rendered ISML) as the shipped storefront; PWA Kit / composable storefront (React on Managed Runtime) for headless over SCAPI

snippets.critic2_persona: senior solution architect who has delivered several Salesforce B2C Commerce projects, is Salesforce-certified for B2C Commerce, knows SFRA and the cartridge path in detail, and can distinguish B2C Commerce standard from a LINK cartridge, from B2B Commerce on the Salesforce Platform, and from custom work
snippets.docs_domains: developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce (B2C Commerce developer guide, SCAPI reference, OCAPI reference, the dw.* Script API reference, Page Designer developer guide, PWA Kit and Managed Runtime docs), help.salesforce.com (Business Manager administration, quota and job configuration), github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud (sfra, pwa-kit, sfcc-ci, sgmf-scripts - the SFRA repository release notes are the reliable version source for the base cartridge), salesforce.com for editions and licensing. Note: much of the developer documentation is gated or version-scoped - always record which compatibility mode a statement applies to.
snippets.best_practice: never modify app_storefront_base - override by placing a same-path file in a cartridge that sits earlier in the site's cartridge path, and prefer server.append / server.prepend over server.replace so later middleware survives; keep business logic in cartridge/scripts and models, controllers thin, ISML free of logic; call external systems only through dw.svc.LocalServiceRegistry service profiles with configured timeout, rate limit and circuit breaker, never a raw HTTP client in a storefront request; extend platform objects with custom attributes declared in metadata rather than custom objects where the object already exists, and respect the custom-object quotas; build editorial content as Page Designer components (component JSON plus a render script and ISML) so business users can edit it, instead of hard-coding it into templates; move anything bulk or slow into the Job Framework; treat <iscache> and personalised-cache decisions as architecture, because page cache is the main performance lever on this platform.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: compatibility mode and API-line facts (SCAPI vs OCAPI status per feature, SFRA base version, deprecations), plus what the quota framework actually enforces in the release in scope. D2: is the claimed standard counterpart really in the SFRA base cartridge, or is it a partner LINK cartridge, a separately licensed product (Einstein, Omnichannel Inventory, Salesforce OMS) or custom. D3: does B2C Commerce standard really cover it - and if the requirement is B2B, is the honest answer B2B Commerce on the Salesforce Platform or custom work, since the two products are separate. D4: exact SCAPI resource and version names, the Page Designer component-to-frontend mapping for a headless target, and any claim that implies direct database access, arbitrary background processes or unbounded API calls.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: check rather than assume: B2B in general - organisation hierarchies, budgets, approval workflows, quotes, punchout and contract pricing are NOT in B2C Commerce; the honest answer is usually B2B Commerce on the Salesforce Platform (a separate product and licence) or custom, and complex B2B is a poor fit; customer-specific and contract pricing beyond price books and customer groups; live ERP price and stock calls inside a storefront request (quota- and latency-bound); inventory beyond the shipped inventory lists (Omnichannel Inventory is separately licensed - verify); complex product configurators and made-to-order products; subscriptions and recurring orders; tax determination beyond a LINK tax cartridge; document downloads and invoices; installed base and equipment; order management, returns and RMA beyond the basic OMS (Salesforce Order Management is a separate product - verify); B2B-style self-service portals; Einstein-dependent requirements where Einstein is not licensed.
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: check before committing: the QUOTA FRAMEWORK - API call, object-count, collection-size and script-execution quotas are enforced per request and per job, and a design that loops over large collections or calls a service per line item hits them (verify current limits in Administration > Operations > Quota Status for the release in scope); NO direct database access - all data goes through the dw.* Script API, SCAPI/OCAPI or IMPEX WebDAV, so any requirement assuming SQL or a reporting database needs an external data platform; NO arbitrary background processes - only the Job Framework with scheduled, quota-bounded steps, so event-driven or near-real-time processing needs an external orchestrator; code is deployed as CODE VERSIONS into numbered slots and activated per instance, so hotfix, rollback and release processes must be designed around that model, and no per-file deployment exists; custom object count and attribute limits; CARTRIDGE PATH COLLISIONS when partner LINK cartridges and project cartridges provide the same file - the earlier cartridge wins silently and a path reorder changes behaviour with no code change; PAGE DESIGNER COMPONENT MAPPING for a headless frontend - SCAPI /shopper/experience returns the page and component tree as JSON and the frontend must render every component type, so each custom component type needs a frontend counterpart or it does not render; session-based custom state (dw.system.Session) has no equivalent in the stateless SCAPI model; feature availability differs by edition and licence (Einstein, Page Designer, Omnichannel Inventory, headless - verify each).
snippets.content_model_notes: Three mechanisms, deliberately kept apart. (1) CONTENT ASSETS (dw.content.Content) are library-scoped rich-text records with custom attributes and folder classification; they render only where a template or a slot includes them, so an asset alone is not a page. (2) CONTENT SLOTS are Business-Manager-configured slot configurations (global, category, folder or product context) bound to a rendering template - powerful for merchandising, but configured outside the repository and template-rendered, which means no headless render contract. (3) PAGE DESIGNER is the component model: cartridge/experience/components/<group>/<component>.json plus a render script and ISML, with pages and layouts under experience/pages and experience/layouts. SCAPI /shopper/experience returns the page and component tree as JSON, so a headless frontend needs a component-type-to-frontend-component map exactly as a Spartacus target does; a custom component type without a frontend counterpart does not render. Region and component visibility rules and the component's editable attribute schema live in the component JSON. Content search goes through dw.content.ContentSearchModel. Standard component names must be verified against the app_storefront_base cartridge of the target SFRA release - they change between releases.
snippets.api_families_hint: see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families - SCAPI Shopper and Admin/Data families plus the legacy OCAPI paths; resource versions (v1/v2) must be verified per release

as_source.platform: Salesforce Commerce Cloud (B2C Commerce, SFRA or SiteGenesis)
as_source.language_stack: server-side JavaScript (CommonJS) on the Rhino-based script engine, ISML templates, dw.* Script API; SFRA client bundle in JS/SCSS built with sgmf-scripts/webpack; SiteGenesis uses pipelines instead of controllers
as_source.default_frontend: SFRA server-rendered ISML storefront (SiteGenesis in older projects); PWA Kit for headless
do_not_run: sfcc-ci (any code deploy, code activate, instance upload, data import, job run)
npm run uploadCartridge and any dw.json-driven WebDAV upload
code-version activation or site import in Business Manager
any IMPEX upload or job execution on a live instance

snippets.version_markers: cartridges/app_storefront_base/package.json version is the SFRA BASE VERSION - the single most useful marker; the absence of app_storefront_base together with pipeline files (*.xml pipelines, app_storefront_core / app_storefront_controllers cartridges) means SiteGenesis, a different and much older architecture. Root package.json: sgmf-scripts version, build scripts, and the paths map that hints at the developer's cartridge setup. Each cartridge's .project gives its NAME as the platform sees it. dw.json (if committed - it should not be) names the instance and the code version used in development. CRITICAL: the COMPATIBILITY MODE (the API/behaviour level the code version runs under) is set per code version in Business Manager and is NOT in the repository - it must be requested, because deprecation and API-behaviour statements depend on it.
snippets.active_units_config: AUTHORITATIVE = the site's CARTRIDGE PATH, configured per site in Business Manager (Administration > Sites > Manage Sites > <site> > Settings > Cartridges) plus the separate Business Manager cartridge path. It is NOT in the repository. Two consequences: a cartridge present under cartridges/ but absent from the path is DEAD, and the ORDER of the path decides which of two same-path files wins. A code-only analysis must therefore request the cartridge path string for every site AND the currently active code version before calling anything dead or asserting which override is effective; the paths entry in the root package.json reflects only the developer's local setup. Site-scoped data (catalogs, slots, jobs, services, preferences) additionally lives in sites/site_template/** and metadata/** as import files, which may or may not match the live instance - say which you read.
snippets.package_sources: root package.json (devDependencies sgmf-scripts, build tooling) and each cartridge's package.json (which declares the cartridge's hooks file and main). Cartridge naming conventions carry the provenance: app_storefront_base = the SFRA base cartridge (never modify), plugin_* = SFRA plugin cartridges (official or partner), int_* = integration cartridges, bm_* = Business Manager extensions, and a partner LINK cartridge usually ships int_<vendor> plus bm_<vendor> with a LINK version recorded in its README or a version file - record that version, because LINK cartridges are the usual source of both functionality and upgrade debt. modules/ holds CommonJS modules resolved as */cartridge/... requires.
snippets.override_mechanisms: overridden = CARTRIDGE PATH RESOLUTION. The cartridge path is an ordered, colon-separated list; for any path-relative resource (a script required as */cartridge/scripts/x.js, an ISML template, a form definition, a properties file) the FIRST cartridge in the path that contains that path wins. So an override is a same-path file in a cartridge placed earlier than app_storefront_base - there is no declaration anywhere, only position. COLLISION SEMANTICS to name per finding: (1) two cartridges both earlier than base providing the same file - the earlier one wins SILENTLY, no error, and reordering the path changes behaviour with no code change; (2) a properties resource file wins as a WHOLE FILE, not per key, so an override must re-declare every key it needs or keys silently disappear (verify for the release); (3) hooks are ADDITIVE - all cartridges registering the same extension point run in path order, so a hook chain's behaviour also depends on path order, and a single-return hook contract makes only the first result count (name which contract applies). extended = the SFRA middleware pattern: a controller file re-declares a named route and uses server.append or server.prepend to add middleware, reaching the previous implementation via module.superModule; server.replace is a HARD override that silently drops the middleware of cartridges later in the path. hooked = package.json "hooks" pointing at cartridge/hooks.json, registering extension points such as dw.ocapi.shop.*, dw.ocapi.data.*, app.payment.processor.*, dw.order.calculate and dw.system.request.* (verify the exact list for the release). ISML overrides = a same-path templates/default/**/*.isml file in an earlier cartridge, plus <isinclude> local and remote includes; a remote include has its own cache and its own request. NOT extensible: dw.* platform API classes cannot be subclassed - only wrapped; platform objects are extended by CUSTOM ATTRIBUTES declared in metadata, not in code.
snippets.schema_sources: metadata/system-objecttype-extensions.xml - custom attributes added to system objects (Product, Variant, Customer, Profile, Order, Basket, SitePreferences, Category, ...): this is the real data-model delta and the attribute groups also drive the Business Manager UI. metadata/custom-objecttype-definitions.xml - custom object types (mind the storage quotas). metadata/services.xml - service definitions, profiles and credentials for LocalServiceRegistry (timeouts, rate limits, circuit breakers). cartridge/forms/default/*.xml - form definitions with validation. cartridge/templates/resources/*.properties - message keys (path-resolved as whole files). sites/site_template/** - catalogs, price books, inventory lists, promotions, campaigns, coupons, slot configurations, customer groups, content library and site preferences as import XML. NOTE: metadata files in the repository are import artefacts, not a guarantee of the live instance state - the instance may carry attributes never committed.
snippets.workflow_sources: there is no BPM engine. Scheduled and bulk work is the JOB FRAMEWORK: job definitions in metadata/jobs.xml or sites/site_template/jobs.xml (flows, steps, schedules, exit statuses) plus steptypes.json in cartridges declaring CUSTOM step types and their parameters, with the step implementations under cartridge/scripts/jobs/**. Order lifecycle is dw.order.Order status setters driven by controllers, hooks (app.payment.processor.*) and jobs, usually handing off to an external OMS - so the real process is split between the platform and the OMS and must be described as such. Storefront-triggered async work does not exist beyond jobs; near-real-time needs an external orchestrator.
snippets.data_script_sources: sites/site_template/** import XML (catalog, pricebook, inventory, promotions, content, customer groups, slot configuration, preferences) and metadata/**.xml; job steps reading and writing files on the IMPEX WebDAV share through dw.io (a job that reads /on/demandware.servlet/webdav/Sites/Impex/... is a data interface, so record the file contract); import/export scripts under cartridge/scripts/**; payloads pushed with sfcc-ci data import. A feed file format defined only inside a job script is a hidden integration contract - name it.
snippets.read_order: root package.json and dw.json, then each cartridge's .project for the platform-visible names and package.json for hooks and main, then per cartridge: cartridge/controllers/** (SFRA routes and middleware, or pipelines for SiteGenesis), cartridge/models/**, cartridge/scripts/**, cartridge/hooks.json, cartridge/templates/default/** plus templates/resources/*.properties, cartridge/forms/**, cartridge/experience/** (Page Designer components, pages, layouts), cartridge/client/** (SFRA JS/SCSS build), steptypes.json, then metadata/** and sites/site_template/**, and finally app_storefront_base for the base implementation actually being overridden. THEN request from the client, because none of it is in the repository: the cartridge path per site, the active code version, the compatibility mode, the effective site preferences and the current quota status.
snippets.hosting_constraints: multi-tenant SaaS - accept these as hard boundaries and mark them not verifiable from the repository. No server, shell or file-system access beyond the IMPEX/Cartridges WebDAV shares. No direct database access: data reaches the outside only through the dw.* API, SCAPI/OCAPI, IMPEX files or jobs. No arbitrary background processes: only Job Framework jobs on schedules, each bounded by quotas and a maximum runtime. Code is deployed as CODE VERSIONS into numbered slots and then ACTIVATED per instance, with rollback by re-activating the previous version - there is no per-file deploy. The QUOTA FRAMEWORK enforces API call counts, collection sizes, object counts and script limits per request and per job; warnings become enforced errors over time, so a design must be quota-aware rather than merely functional (verify the current limits for the release). Request timeouts forbid long-running storefront requests. Page cache (<iscache>, personalised cache) is the main performance lever and is part of the architecture, not an optimisation. Instance topology is sandbox / development / staging / production with data replication between them, so environment parity and data refresh are project concerns. Einstein, Page Designer, Omnichannel Inventory and headless access are edition- or licence-dependent (verify).
